newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares start week firm, DAX over 2,700.
newsitem.headline: German shares start week firm, DAX over 2,700.

text.p: German shares got the week off to a solid start on Monday as the firm dollar and a stream of positive corporate news helped ease the tension which sparked sharp market declines last week.
Heavyweight blue chip companies including Daimler-Benz and BASF led an advance which added more than one percent to the 30-share DAX index.

The DAX ended floor dealings up 29.61 points at 2,703.83, comfortably above the psychologically-crucial 2,700 level and the IBIS DAX index which tracks later electronic dealings held the gains to close at 2,703.33.

Daimler-Benz gained 2.47 marks to 89.90 marks in bourse trade and ended late dealings at 89.85 as the market took a positive slant on a magazine article which said its chairman Juergen Schrempp had threatened to resign in order to force through a company restructure.
Although Daimler denied the report, dealers gave it some credence and said it proved Daimler was really committed to restructuring in shareholders' interests.
Merger news boosted interest in chemicals.

BASF rose on news it had agreed a joint venture with Dutch firm DSM on polyester resins, a move analysts said was logical in view of consolidation in the sector. The chemicals group ended late trade at 49, up 1.45 marks.
Meanwhile preferred shares in consumer products Henkel advanced 60 pfennigs to 68.90 marks after it said it planned a full takeover of U.S. firm Loctite, of which it now already 35 percent.
Other big advancers included Volkswagen, which gained 2.50 marks to 597.50 over the day after the government said it planned to liberalise laws regarding its shareholder rights.
Engineering group Deutsche Babcock rebounded strongly from weakness sparked by insolvency rumours last week, gaining more than five percent to 42.50 marks over the day.
Retailer Metro fell 1.70 marks at 128.20, paring a decline which sent it as low as 123.50 after reports of a probe into irregularities in its share propspectus was unjustified.
Metro issued a statement mid-morning to say a loss carried over, the alleged subject of the probe, had been approved.
